- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward momentum.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 68.27 → 69.51) are common, suggesting model fails to account for post-spike consolidation or reversal.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to prior levels too quickly, underestimating volatility or trend persistence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts show persistent lag in capturing true price direction, especially in the middle-to-late period (days 15–30).
- Model underestimates late-period price surges (e.g., 71.56–75.94), suggesting it fails to anticipate policy or market-driven catalysts in the final 10 days.
- Forecasts often ignore recent low-price corrections (e.g., 64.26–64.86) and overreact to short-term volatility.
